findings.name: Trend verdict
findings.definition: The trend is the dominant direction of price over months, read from swing highs and lows, the slope of the lines through them, and where price sits against its long averages. Bullish means higher highs and higher lows. Bearish means lower highs and lower lows. Range-bound means neither side is winning.
findings.meaning: The trend verdict is bearish. Swing structure is lower highs and lower lows (0 higher highs, 0 higher lows, 2 lower highs, 2 lower lows across the last 6 swings). The two trend lines form a diverging lines (expanding, broadening shape). Price $674.57 sits below its 50-day average and below its 200-day average.
findings.confirms: The verdict strengthens if price breaks the last swing point in the trend direction and holds it on a close.
findings.invalidates: A close through the last swing point against the trend, held for two sessions, ends this verdict and the structure gets re-read.

findings.name: Moving average stack
findings.definition: Moving averages smooth price over a set number of days. When the short averages sit above the long ones in order, buyers have been in control at every horizon. The reverse stack means sellers have.
findings.meaning: The averages are not in a clean stack, so the timeframes disagree. Price is below the 50-day, below the 200-day.
findings.confirms: The stack holding while price rides the shortest average confirms it.
findings.invalidates: Averages crossing out of order ends the stack read.

findings.name: Golden cross (SMA 50 over SMA 200)
findings.definition: A cross of the 50-day average through the 200-day average. It marks the moment the medium trend overtook the long trend. It is a slow signal: it confirms a turn more often than it starts one.
findings.meaning: No such cross in the last year of data. The 50-day is at $717.76 and the 200-day at $682.21
findings.confirms: The 50-day crossing the 200-day is the event itself.
findings.invalidates: Nothing to invalidate: the event has not happened.

findings.name: Death cross (SMA 50 under SMA 200)

findings.name: RSI 14
findings.definition: The Relative Strength Index measures the speed of recent gains against recent losses, on a 0 to 100 scale. Above 70 is called overbought, below 30 oversold. It describes momentum, not value.
findings.meaning: RSI is 41.3, neutral. Divergence check against the last two swing lows: none.
findings.confirms: For a reversal read, RSI crossing back through 30 from below, or a divergence that price then confirms with a higher low.
findings.invalidates: RSI staying pinned at an extreme while price trends through it: in a strong trend, extremes can persist and the mean-reversion read fails.

findings.name: MACD 12, 26, 9
findings.definition: MACD compares two exponential averages of price. The MACD line crossing its signal line marks momentum changing hands. The histogram is the gap between them: widening means the move is accelerating, narrowing means it is tiring.
findings.meaning: MACD is -13.34, signal -12.91, histogram -0.43 and narrowing. No cross in the last 10 sessions.
findings.confirms: A fresh cross in the trend direction, with the histogram expanding.
findings.invalidates: A cross back the other way, or the histogram flipping sign.

findings.name: Bollinger Bands 20, 2
findings.definition: Bollinger Bands wrap price in a channel two standard deviations wide around its 20-day average. Percent B says where price sits inside that channel: 1 is the top band, 0 the bottom, outside either means price is walking the band in a strong trend. Bandwidth measures volatility: a squeeze, bandwidth at its lowest quarter of the year, often precedes a large move.
findings.meaning: Price is inside the bands: upper $739.35, middle $695.18, lower $651.02, percent B 0.27, bandwidth 12.7 percent. Squeeze: no.
findings.confirms: A band walk that keeps closing outside the band confirms trend strength. A squeeze confirms when price breaks the range it built.
findings.invalidates: Two closes back inside the band end a band walk read.

findings.name: Stochastic 14, 3
findings.definition: The stochastic oscillator places today's close inside the last 14 days' range. Percent K is the fast line, percent D its average. Crosses under 20 are read as momentum turning up from washed-out; crosses over 80 as momentum turning down from stretched.
findings.meaning: Percent K is 47.2, percent D 45.9. No cross in the last 5 sessions.
findings.confirms: The cross itself is the confirmation; price then has to take out the prior day's high to follow through.
findings.invalidates: Percent K falling back under percent D after a bullish cross kills it.

findings.name: Gap down on 2026-10-22
findings.definition: A gap is a jump between one day's close and the next day's range, leaving empty price space. Breakaway gaps leave a base, runaway gaps sit mid-move, exhaustion gaps print at the end of a move and stall. An unfilled gap is open price space price often revisits.
findings.meaning: On 2026-10-22 the stock gapped down: the gap zone is $715.43 to $719.71. Class: breakaway (it left a flat base). It is filled.
findings.confirms: An unfilled gap in the trend direction that price refuses to revisit confirms the move's urgency.
findings.invalidates: A filled gap loses its information; the zone becomes ordinary price.

findings.name: Climax volume day
findings.definition: A climax day trades at least twice the normal volume. It marks a crowd event: capitulation at a low or blow-off at a high. One climax day does not end a move, but it says the move just spent real energy.

findings.confirms: A climax at a low that price then holds, with a higher low after it, is the classic capitulation sequence.
findings.invalidates: Price slicing through the climax day's low on ordinary volume makes the climax just another down day.

findings.name: Dow Theory read
findings.definition: Dow Theory, the oldest trend framework: a primary trend is a sequence of higher highs and higher lows (up) or lower highs and lower lows (down). It is confirmed when price closes beyond the last swing point in the trend direction, and volume should expand in the direction of the primary trend. Secondary reactions against it are noise until they break the sequence.
findings.meaning: Primary trend: down (lower highs and lower lows). Confirmation event: none. Volume confirmation: yes, volume expands in the primary direction.
findings.confirms: Each new swing extending the sequence, on expanding volume, confirms it.
findings.invalidates: A close beyond the last swing point against the primary trend, followed by a failed retest, ends the Dow read.

findings.name: Elliott Wave count
findings.definition: Elliott Wave theory says moves unfold in counted waves: five in the trend direction (the impulse), three against it (the correction, labeled A, B, C). The C leg often measures a Fibonacci extension of the A leg. It is an interpretation framework, never a fact: the same swings can carry more than one honest count.
findings.meaning: INTERPRETATION, not fact: the five swings from 2026-07-29 can be counted as an impulse up: 2026-07-29 $661.14, 2026-08-17 $734.58, 2026-09-16 $700.00, 2026-10-06 $762.86, 2026-11-05 $647.05. If the count is right, that directional move is a complete or nearly complete impulse and a three-wave correction follows or is underway.
findings.confirms: A three-wave correction after this impulse, turning at a Fibonacci extension, supports the count.
findings.invalidates: A close back through the wave 4 point at $762.86 breaks this count.

findings.name: Fibonacci retracement of the major advance
findings.definition: Fibonacci retracement divides a completed move by fixed ratios (23.6, 38.2, 50, 61.8, 78.6 percent) to map where a pullback often pauses. It is a level map, not a signal: the levels matter because many traders watch the same ones, and because they land on real shelves.
findings.meaning: Measured from the low $555.60 on 2026-03-30 to the high $762.86 on 2026-10-06. Price at $674.57 has retraced 42.6 percent of the advance. Levels price has touched and reacted at: 0.236 ($713.95, 2026-10-15), 0.382 ($683.69, 2026-10-30), 0.5 ($659.23, 2026-11-09). Confluences: 0.382 at $683.69 meets the shelf near $678.78; 0.382 at $683.69 meets the shelf near $682.23; 0.5 at $659.23 meets the shelf near $661.50.
findings.confirms: A level confirms itself when price touches it and reverses with a candle or volume signature.
findings.invalidates: A level that price closes through twice stops being a level on this map and the next one down takes over.

findings.name: Fibonacci retracement of the current decline (bounce map)
findings.definition: The same ratios applied to the current decline, run upward: they map where a bounce most often stalls. A bounce that dies at the 38.2 or 50 percent line is behaving like a countertrend rally, not a reversal.
findings.confirms: A bounce closing through the 61.8 percent line upgrades it from countertrend rally to reversal candidate.
findings.invalidates: New lows extend the leg and every line on this map moves down.

findings.name: Harmonic Gartley
findings.definition: Harmonic patterns measure a five-point swing (X, A, B, C, D) against fixed Fibonacci ratios. When the ratios fit, the zone where D completes, the potential reversal zone, is where the pattern says exhaustion is likeliest. Ratios that do not fit mean the pattern is not there, whatever the shape suggests.
findings.meaning: No swing set in the window fits this pattern's first two ratios (AB/XA and BC/AB) inside tolerance, so there is no honest path to a D point. The shape may look close; the numbers say no.
findings.confirms: A swing set landing AB/XA and BC/AB inside their windows, with price then reaching the projected zone.
findings.invalidates: Nothing to invalidate: the pattern is not there.

findings.name: Island reversal

findings.confirms: The pattern is complete at the second gap; follow-through in the same direction confirms it.
findings.invalidates: Price closing back through the island fills it and ends the read.
